text:
Anna P.: heads up — our eval-runner is producing nondeterministic BERTScore deltas between CPU and quant runs. noticed on the newjenkins job.
Rishi K.: hmm, nondet how large? percent-level or tiny float noise? :thinking_face:
Anna P.: sometimes 0.001, sometimes 0.05 on small calibration sets. failing the calibration CI gate intermittently.
Marco D.: could be serialization or ordering. did you check the payloads sent to the bertscore service?
Anna P.: i diffed a few payloads. looks like the embeddings list order is stable, but floats get truncated differently. runner serializes with numpy float64 -> json then bertscore service parses to float32.
Priya S.: we also saw something similar with BLEU tokenization earlier — subtle dtype and tokenizer config mismatches. maybe the contract isn't strict enough.
Lucy H.: can you paste the snippet that serializes?
Anna P.: sure — here's the minimal repro we used:
```python
# runner payload snippet
payload = {
    "ids": ["ex1", "ex2"],
    "embeddings": embeddings.tolist(),  # numpy array f64
    "meta": {"model": "redwood/opt-quant"}
}
requests.post(BERT_URL, json=payload)
```
Rishi K.: yeah that will put lots of decimals. if bertscore does float32 casting on its side you'll get tiny differences that compound in cosine computations.
Marco D.: two immediate fixes: 1) canonicalize to a fixed dtype (float32) and rounded string representation before json; 2) switch to base64-encoded raw bytes + dtype in the contract to force deterministic decode.
Priya S.: for CI gating we should also add tolerance configs to the metric tests (e.g., atol=1e-3) so small numeric drift doesn't trigger regressions. we already have a pass@k flake elsewhere due to sampling randomness — need to separate randomness from serialization nondet.
Anna P.: agreed. i'll push a small runner patch to force embeddings = embeddings.astype('float32') and use `.tolist()` with numpy.round(..., 6) for now.
Lucy H.: also add a test in eval-runner unit tests that serializes and deserializes and asserts exact equality of the decoded bytes or close within tol.
Rishi K.: could we also change the bertscore service to accept `encoding: "float32-base64"` and check dtype header? that would make cross-lang callers safe.
Marco D.: i can prototype the server-side acceptance. i'll add a compatibility branch: if payload has `dtype` and `base64` prefer decode path, else fallback to json floats with a warning log.
Anna P.: note: this surfaced a second unrelated issue — pass@k scoring is off by one when dedup filter runs after sampling. small note for the metrics owners.
Priya S.: oh yeah, dedup post-filtering reduces k effectively. need to compute pass@k on the post-processed candidate set or use sampling-without-replacement logic. opened a ticket last month — i'll link it.
Anna P.: thanks. for the immediate fix i'm going to: (a) enforce float32+rounding in runner, (b) add unit test for serialization equality, (c) add CI smoke to run a tiny calibration set with bertscore and assert stability.
eval-bot: smoke-evals/job-421: FAILED — nondeterministic bertscore delta > 0.02 on calibration set (run 7).
Lucy H.: @anna want help with the unit test? i can add a hermetic runner->server integration test using a local docker bertscore binary.
Anna P.: yes please. also @rishi @marco can you review the server compat patch when ready?
Rishi K.: yep. i'll write up the contract change in the repo README (metrics-contract.md) so other teams know encoding options.
Marco D.: I'll prototype base64 path today. once we have that, we can gradually migrate callers and flip a feature flag.
Priya S.: and i'll adjust the CI gating thresholds and add a note to the dashboards: "bertscore: comparisons should use stable serialization; small deltas tolerated up to 1e-3".
Anna P.: cool. timeline: patch + tests tomorrow morning, server branch Tues, CI tolerance update Wed. tagging this thread for follow-up. :white_check_mark:
